# Excel LTSC advanced print-layout reference review — 2026-11-23

**Inputs:** `print-layout.xlsx` from the PR #15 PDF visual fixture and a PDF independently exported on Windows using Microsoft Excel LTSC. Compared with the `print-layout-library.pdf` generated by ExcelExportKit's opt-in `PdfUseWorksheetPrintSettings` renderer.

## Observed results

| Check | Microsoft Excel LTSC | ExcelExportKit | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page size and orientation | A4 landscape (841.9 × 595.3 pt) | A4 landscape (841.9 × 595.3 pt) | Match |
| Total PDF pages | 4 | 4 | Match |
| Pages 1 and 2 | Section/Item, first 16 then last 16 items | Same | Match |
| Pages 3 and 4 | Score/Status, first 16 then last 16 records | Same | Match |
| Repeated title rows | Two per printed section | Two per printed section | Match |
| Values and labels | All 32 items, scores and statuses retained | Same | Match |
| Print scale/spacing | Compact Excel grid in upper-left | PDF table expands across much of page | **Visual mismatch** |
| Additional title/footer | None | Fixture adds document title and page counter | Intentional option mismatch |

The independently exported PDF metadata identifies **Microsoft Excel LTSC** as the creator/producer. It was supplied by the workbook exporter and is not committed to GitHub.

**Content verification:** All 32 distinct item numbers, their 32 scores, and their 32 statuses are present, with consistent ordering and distribution across pages. The horizontal and vertical manual breaks produce the same four section pages, and title rows appear per section.

**Geometry verification:** Excel positions the grid close to the upper-left with substantially smaller content bounds. ExcelExportKit's table layout uses relative-width columns filling much more of the printable page, and row spacing and type size differ. Matching page count and page-break order do **not** establish exact sizing, margin fidelity or 85%-scale geometry.

## Recommendation

- Keep existing feature opt-in and retain documentation that the print renderer is an approximation rather than pixel-identical Microsoft Excel.
- Do **not** change default layout/pagination merely to make this synthetic fixture look identical. That would introduce regressions and cannot reproduce the full Excel print engine.
- The automated `print-layout` fixture now asserts page count and page-section text ordering, guarding the behavior that both renderers agree on.
- Before stable v2.0.0 publication, retain the **real-world workbook** gate and verify any hosting application imposes timeouts and concurrency limits for untrusted workbooks.
- Optional future work: a separate experimental layout mode with explicit physical column widths, row heights, scaling and margins, followed by independent print-reference tests.

**Conclusion:** For this synthetic workbook, data fidelity, orientation and manual print-section mapping pass. Exact visual print fidelity remains **not supported**. These results are a scoped verification of the documented approximate layout contract, not an endorsement of pixel-perfect parity.
